content: Qwen3-Reranker CPU latency is structural: causal-LM yes/no logit = full forward pass per (query,doc) pair. Measured: ~1s/chunk on CPU-only Linux server (qmd issue #264, the project SIF ports): 20-30 chunks = 34-49s per collection per search, unusable for interactive/AI-assistant workflows; their fix was skip-rerank hybrid (25-35x faster, ~1.3s). M1 Pro CPU ~580ms/candidate, 18 candidates=10.4s, 50 candidates crash/timeout. Another CPU run: 10 docs=2.6s, 50=13.8s, 100=crash at 3.9GB RAM. Even on H100, qwen3-4b >1s per 100-candidate query; single-forward-pass rerankers (gte-modernbert 149M) are fundamentally faster than autoregressive yes/no scoring. Implication: cap rerank candidates ~10-20 on CPU, expose latency budget, make rerank opt-in/skippable for interactive paths. Sources: github tobi/qmd issue 264, github cried-nutty-won/rag-system (M1 Pro numbers), dev.to production RAG 2025-08 (CPU/T4 breakdown), aimultiple reranker benchmark.
